reason: The heat store needs a tank, but the available parts do not make its construction sequence clear. Checking the steel should identify a useful starting connection.
expectation: The inspection should reveal which available parts can form a tank or heat-recovery component.

alternatives.reason: The tool might shape the steel into a tank, but its compatibility is uncertain.

effect: The steel and service tool made a vented tank for non-potable heating water; it still needs a separate coolant coil.
reaction: The automatic construction was useful, and the separation of coolant from tank water is clear.
reason: The coolant tubing should form the separate coil inside the tank.
expectation: The tubing will be fitted as a heat-exchange coil in the tank.

effect: The tank now has a sealed coolant coil, leaving it ready for heating water.
reaction: The separate fluid paths make the heat exchange easy to understand.
reason: The tank needs water around the coil to store heat.
expectation: The tank will fill with water that can absorb heat from the coil.

effect: The water supply did not combine with the coiled tank, so I need another preparation or connection first.
reaction: That was unexpected; the tank still appears to need water.
reason: The coil needs a connection to the process heat loop, so I will try installing the tank at the heat-recovery connection.
expectation: The tank will connect to the heat-recovery loop, possibly after other required preparation.

alternatives.reason: Insulating the tank may be required before connecting it.

effect: The attempted connection automatically insulated the tank, which is now ready for water.
reaction: The required insulation before filling was unexpected, but the feedback made the next step clear.
reason: The insulated tank is explicitly ready for water to store heat.
expectation: The tank will fill with water around the separate coolant coil.

effect: The insulated tank is filled with water around the separate coil and is ready for a heat source.
reaction: The separate fluid paths remain clear.
reason: The indoor heat-recovery connection should supply process heat to the tank's coil.
expectation: The coil will connect to the process loop and heat the stored water.

effect: Connecting the filled tank to the process loop stored heat in its water and completed the goal.
reaction: The thermostat and separate coolant coil made the finished system feel physically sensible.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the heating coil was most worthwhile: it showed how process coolant can transfer heat to stored water without mixing the fluids.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to fill the coiled tank before insulating it was an unsuccessful detour; the need to insulate first was not apparent.

surprise.text: The attempted heat-loop connection automatically fitted the insulation instead, revealing the required next preparation.

arbitrary.text: Requiring insulation before filling felt somewhat arbitrary: the result explained why insulation helps, but not why the tank could not be filled first.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for the practical making and the discovery story, although I would hope future construction sequences make prerequisites clearer.
